abstraction_design.rationale: The components are sensibly sized for the app and stretch to most cases, but several abstractions exist and are bypassed (TypeBadge) or grow flags (PokemonGrid), and the per-resource page loaders are structured copy-paste rather than a reusable skeleton.

findings.issue: Loaders and components are typed with `any` even though tsconfig includes `.react-router/types`; the framework's generated Route.LoaderArgs/Route.ComponentProps are unused, so refactors of the loader-data shape in api.server.ts compile fine and break at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Use `import type { Route } from './+types/<route>'` with Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps / Route.MetaArgs, and type the getXPage return values so the compiler guides data-shape changes.

findings.issue: The not-found flow (`data ?? { notFound: true }`, a meta() special case, and an early `return <NotFoundPage/>`) is hand-rolled and duplicated in four routes, and responds with HTTP 200 instead of 404.
findings.suggestion: Follow the framework pattern: throw `data('Not Found', { status: 404 })` from the loader and render one shared ErrorBoundary/NotFound (or at minimum extract a single helper for the sentinel + meta), so the behaviour lives in one place.

findings.issue: Type-badge markup (`type-badge type-${name}`) is inlined in five places although a TypeBadge component exists at components.tsx:34-39.
findings.suggestion: Give TypeBadge an optional `to` (link) variant and use it everywhere, so badge styling/structure changes in one file.

findings.issue: getAbilityPage re-implements cardFromPokemonRef + unique-by-id + dex sort instead of reusing cardsFromRefs (:158-168); a change to card building or ordering must be applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsFromRefs to pass an extra flag through (or accept a mapper) and use it for ability pages too, keeping one card-list builder.

findings.issue: `Card` in components.tsx is a hand-maintained structural duplicate of `PokemonCard`; the two will drift.
findings.suggestion: Export PokemonCard from (or move the type into) a shared module and have the component import it.

findings.issue: Caching is spread across several module-level promises (typeInfos, generations, speciesIndex, homeData, versionGroups) plus a never-evicting recordCache (:14-19); there is no single cache-policy seam, and changing rules (TTL, eviction) means reworking each one.
findings.suggestion: Introduce one memoize helper with an explicit policy (e.g. `cached(key, ttl, fn)`) and route every cached value through it so caching rules have a single knob.

findings.issue: PokemonGrid already has `showTypes` and optional `hidden` prop flags; the next card variation (e.g. sorting control or extra metadata) adds more booleans.
findings.suggestion: Either keep the grid dumb and pass prepared rows, or split card content into a small slot/variant prop before the flag list grows.

findings.issue: navigateWithParam and onSearch duplicate the same URLSearchParams-mutation dance (delete `page`, set/delete the key, preventScrollReset).
findings.suggestion: Have onSearch call navigateWithParam('q', value, true) so query-param handling is written once.

findings.issue: The route file mixes the page layout with the MovesTable component and its sorting state machine, making it the largest and least navigable file in the app.
findings.suggestion: Move MovesTable (and its Column/sort types) into its own module under routes/ or components/.

summary: This is a small, tidy app with an unusually good data-layer seam: everything that knows about the API (base URL, caching, sprites, card building) lives in one server-only module, so the realistic fixes — the Deoxys-style sprite bug, base-URL or cache changes, card-list ordering — each land in a single obvious file. What keeps it from being exemplary is pervasive `any` typing on loader boundaries, a hand-rolled 404 sentinel copy-pasted into four routes instead of the framework's ErrorBoundary pattern, and small duplications (inline type-badge markup, a second card-list builder, a duplicated Card type) that a future maintainer must remember to fix in N places. Most extension work (an Items section) is structured copy-paste rather than reuse, but the pattern is consistent enough to be safe.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: API_BASE_URL and the record cache are defined exactly once (:9, :14-19), so both changes touch one file; the catch is that caching is implemented in several distinct forms (recordCache plus five module-level memoized promises with no eviction), so changing the *policy* requires understanding the whole 500-line data module.
